title: A Novel Framework Linking Cortical Circuitry, Visual Auras, Neurovascular Coupling and Migraine
content: Visual auras, such as the zigzag lines known as fortifications, are frequent prodromal symptoms of migraine headaches. Visual auras themselves have been claimed to be due to a traveling wave of cortical spreading depression (CSD) across the visual cortex. However, since the auras and the headache can happen independently and it has been impractical to observe CSD in humans during an aura, any causal connection between the aura or the CSD and the headaches has been under question. Attempts at explaining the fortifications as arising from the orientation column structure of the visual cortex has also been challenging. Here, on the basis of the circuit operations underpinning visual cortical orientation selectivity and functional architecture as arising from patterns of feature selectivity present in the geniculate signals to the cortex, we explain the intriguing zigzag pattern of fortifications, other types of auras and a causal relationship between CSD and headaches.
